'''Judith Rousseau''' is a [[Bayesian statistics|Bayesian statistician]] who studies [[Frequentist inference|frequentist]] properties of Bayesian methods.{{r|sv}} She is a professor of statistics at [[Université Paris-Dauphine]]. She was previously a professor at the [[University of Oxford]], a Fellow of [[Jesus College, Oxford]],{{r|jc}} and a professor at [[ENSAE Paris]]. She a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]{{r|fims}} and a Fellow of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]].{{r|isba}}

==Education and career==
Rousseau studied statistics and economics at [[ENSAE ParisTech]], starting in pure mathematics but changing fields after taking a statistics class "because of all the interactions it has with other fields".{{r|sv}} She completed a doctorate in 1997 at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]]. Her dissertation, ''Asymptotic properties of Bayes estimators'', was supervised by [[Christian Robert]].{{r|jc|mgp}}

She taught at [[Paris Descartes University]] from 1998 to 2004, [[Paris-Dauphine University]] beginning in 2004, and (while on leave from Paris-Dauphine) at ENSAE from 2009 to 2014.{{r|jc}} She became Professor of Statistics at Oxford in 2017{{r|oxon}}, then returned to Paris-Dauphine in 2023.

==Recognition==
In 2015 Rousseau won the inaugural [[Ethel Newbold]] Prize of the [[Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability]].
The award recognizes a "recipient of any gender who is an outstanding statistical scientist for a body of work that represents excellence in research in mathematical statistics". The body of work for which Rousseau was recognized includes her work on infinite-dimensional variants of the [[Bernstein–von Mises theorem]].{{r|sv}}

In 2019, she was awarded a [[European Research Council]] (ERC) Advance Grant for her project "General theory for Big Bayes".

As of 2026, she is president-elect of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]].
